description: Indiana WIC helps eligible pregnant and postpartum women, infants and young children with food and nutrition support. Enrollment starts with a local clinic appointment.
introduction: Indiana WIC helps eligible pregnant and postpartum women, infants and young children with food and nutrition support. Enrollment starts with a local clinic appointment.

sections.who: Applicants must live in Indiana, meet the income test and have nutritional risk assessed by a health professional. Categories include pregnancy, breastfeeding through the baby’s first birthday, non-breastfeeding postpartum women through six months, and children younger than five.
sections.get: WIC offers selected healthy foods, nutrition screening and education, breastfeeding support and referrals. Indiana uses eWIC food benefits. Your clinic explains the food package for each participant.
sections.docs:
• Identification for the caregiver and applicants, plus proof of address.
  • Income evidence for household members, including recent pay records, or qualifying Medicaid, SNAP or TANF enrollment evidence.
  • Immunization records for children applying who are younger than two.
sections.apply:
1. Find your clinic

    Use the state application page to arrange certification.

  2. Attend certification

    Bring the caregiver, the child applying and the requested records. Staff assess eligibility and nutritional needs.

  3. Learn to use your benefits

    Ask the clinic about the eWIC card, approved foods and follow-up visits.
sections.after: Save clinic contact details and appointment information. Ask before changing a scheduled visit or transferring a child’s case to a new caregiver.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using eligibility requirements, certification instructions, WIC services, client information. The administering provider determines eligibility and availability.

faqs: Can SNAP help with the WIC income check?
Yes. Bring qualifying enrollment evidence; the clinic still checks WIC’s other conditions.
Indiana includes children placed with relatives or foster parents. Ask the clinic about certification even while Medicaid activation is pending.
The state instructs the caregiver and the infant or child applying to attend.
Is WIC a general grocery allowance?
No. Purchases are limited to the participant’s approved WIC food package.

provenance.review_scope: Published eligibility and intake facts; no inferred payment guarantees.
